spiritual_reading.full_translation: A complete ordering was laid upon the whole domain of spiritual states, that everything in them be brought into full readiness through an entire process, until a sufficient form of enlightened reception was established for conjunction and use. Then attention turned to a particular recipient. When the appointed fullness of illumination and insight was opened in him, the entire range of his knowledges and all their ordered connections were made manifest to his understanding. He was then to turn wholly toward that illumination, and to live within it as his governing life. This life was not to be claimed as arising from his selfhood, but to be held as a higher gift distinct from the three subordinate degrees within him, which stand beneath and must receive in their own order what flows down from above.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the ordering of a whole domain into the interior formation of one recipient who must live from higher influx, not from self.
paragraph_translations.notes: Source is highly fragmentary: the subject of the command, the identity of the ‘seven’ and the ‘particular person,’ and the exact action sequence are unclear. Rendered ‘commanded/made ready’ as imposed spiritual ordering; ‘seven’ as a full process; ‘people of the Light’ as a sufficient form of enlightened reception; ‘universe and all its orders’ as the entire range of knowledges and their connections; final clause treated as distinguishing higher received life from three discrete lower degrees.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Moderately coherent as a single teaching about universal preparation culminating in the illumination of a particular recipient, and the requirement that he live from received wisdom rather than proprium. Coherence weakens where the fragmentary wording makes agency and the function of ‘seven’ and ‘people’ uncertain, but the final emphasis on discrete degrees and non-self-derived life holds a stable doctrinal line.

findings.location: ¶2 (opening clause: “⟨p.284⟩[these five aeons]ll of them [were commanded] that they shall [be made ready] seven people [of the Light]”)
findings.diagnosis: The passage is too damaged to sustain the spiritual reading’s move from “five aeons / commanded / made ready / seven people of the Light” into a smooth correspondential narrative about interior preparation. The reader’s stumble (“identity of the ‘seven’ and the ‘particular person’… unclear”) arises primarily from heavy lacunae plus a likely mismatch of enumerative/administrative framing (“five… seven… people of the Light”) with the later, more interiorized discourse.
findings.evidence: Text is broken and numerative: “⟨p.284⟩[these five aeons]ll of them [were commanded] that they shall [be made ready] seven people [of the Light]”. The spiritual reading explicitly reports the failure points: “Source is highly fragmentary: the subject of the command, the identity of the ‘seven’ and the ‘particular person,’ and the exact action sequence are unclear.” Because the subject and verb-chain are lost, we cannot tell whether “five aeons” govern “seven people,” whether “people” are actors or results, or whether a list/jurisdictional scheme is being introduced. The reader’s interpretive substitutions (“seven as a full process,” “people… as reception”) are not text-driven but compensations for missing syntax.

findings.location: ¶2 (middle seam: “Again, he too, this per[son] the time when [the fullness] of the light [and the wisdom] the universe [and all its orders] is revealed [to him]”)
findings.diagnosis: There is a visible transition/seam (“Again,” then a shift to “he… this person”) where the narrative jumps from a collective commissioning (“five aeons… commanded… made ready…”) to an individualized illumination report. The spiritual reading had to supply the bridge (“Then attention turned to a particular recipient”) because the text no longer preserves the connective tissue. This is not clearly an administrative insertion; it is best explained as a damaged join between two originally coherent correspondential statements (cosmic preparation → personal revelation).
findings.evidence: The seam marker is explicit: “Again, he too, this per[son]…”. The reader notes “agency… unclear” and “exact action sequence… unclear,” which is exactly what happens when a connective clause is lost at a page/line break. Importantly, the content after the seam (“fullness of the light and the wisdom… revealed to him”) supports the reader’s overall interior trajectory; the problem is not alien voice but missing linkage.

findings.location: ¶2 (illumination clause: “the universe [and all its orders] is revealed [to him]”)
findings.diagnosis: This is a clean, substrate-style correspondential moment: disclosure of an ordered totality to a recipient as a functional event (revelation/manifestation), not a roster of administrators. The spiritual reading’s “entire range of his knowledges and all their ordered connections” is a plausible correspondential paraphrase and does not require forcing.
findings.evidence: Text: “the universe [and all its orders] is revealed [to him]”. This teaches by function (revelation makes “orders” intelligible) rather than by governance (no named rulers/jurisdictions). The reader’s coherence report singles out that “the final emphasis… holds a stable doctrinal line,” and this clause is part of that stable line: ordered totality → comprehension/reception.

findings.location: ¶2 (closing: “take to the light [wholly]… the way that he exists [in it] from [not from himself] these other three [degrees within him]”)
findings.diagnosis: This is the chapter’s most coherent substrate teaching: an imperative/description of living “in the light,” explicitly “not from himself,” and distinguishing “three degrees within him.” The spiritual reading’s central doctrinal point (“live from received wisdom rather than proprium… three subordinate degrees”) arises directly from the preserved wording; no administrative overlay is needed to explain the sense.
findings.evidence: Text preserves the key functional relations: “take to the light [wholly]… exists [in it]… [not from himself]… these other three [degrees within him].” This naturally yields a correspondential teaching about influx/derivation (life not self-derived) and ordered interior levels (“three degrees”). The reader explicitly says “the final clause treated as distinguishing higher received life from three discrete lower degrees” and that this “holds a stable doctrinal line”—that stability indicates genuine substrate rather than later systematizing administration.

textual_criticism.summary: 4 findings: the chapter fragment shows no clear administrative overlay that should be excised or even annotated. The spiritual reading stumbled where the Coptic is highly fragmentary and where a damaged seam (“Again… this person…”) forces the reader to supply missing connective logic. The most intact material (revelation of ‘the universe and all its orders’; turning wholly to the light; ‘not from himself’; ‘three degrees’) is clean correspondential substrate.
